day_shape: 80 items: CENTCOM confirms US naval blockade with 17 vessels redirected, Iran executes two Isfahan protesters, Iran-Oman-Saudi-US talks accelerate on reopening Hormuz, Netanyahu-Trump meeting set with Pickaxe Mountain on agenda, heavy Khamenei Hezbollah-letter cycle; UK Parliament silent.

threads.label: Hormuz blockade and reopening talks
threads.summary: CENTCOM said USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. is supporting a US blockade that has redirected 17 commercial vessels, disabled two and boarded two, while Jerusalem Post reported accelerated US-Iran and Iran-Oman talks on a short-term shipping fix. Iran's foreign minister Araghchi spoke with Omani and Saudi counterparts on Hormuz security, and Khatam al-Anbiya HQ warned the blockade amounts to escalation of war.

threads.label: Isfahan protester executions
threads.summary: Iran executed two men, Abolfazl Sepahi Badjanani and Amirhossein Safari Hosseinabadi, at dawn over the January Alikhani Square unrest, with Iran International reporting heavy security and overnight clashes. IRIB denied a claim that a woman had been killed at the same square, calling it fabricated by hostile media.

threads.label: Netanyahu-Trump Washington meeting agenda
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Netanyahu will brief Trump on Iranian activity at Pickaxe Mountain and efforts to rebuild the nuclear programme, with the Saudi nuclear deal and Turkey's F-35s also on the table. Trump said the US is negotiating with Iran and would return to war if talks fail; a Reuters/Ipsos poll put US support for the Iran war at one in three.

threads.label: Khamenei response to Hezbollah letter
threads.summary: Khamenei's office published a three-part rollout of the Supreme Leader's reply to a letter of allegiance from Hezbollah's secretary-general, declaring defence of Hezbollah Lebanon a strategic policy of the Islamic Republic. Defa Press separately quoted Sardar Mir-Ahmadi framing avenging the killed leader as a national security duty.

threads.label: Gaza operations and ISF entry
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed Wael Musa Khaled Ladawi, head of Hamas's internal security in central Gaza, in a Deir al-Balah strike, and demolished a Hamas tunnel spanning hundreds of metres in the north; Islamic Jihad's Amro Abu Alrish was also killed. Times of Israel reported the security cabinet approved limited entry of a 200-strong International Stabilization Force under the Board of Peace plan.

threads.label: Lebanon track and Hezbollah disarmament
threads.summary: A senior US State Department official said the next Israel-Lebanon talks will be held in Rome on 4-6 August, with US officials telling the Jerusalem Post Washington backs a phased IDF withdrawal under a Hezbollah disarmament framework. IRIB cited Al-Nushrah reporting Israeli strikes on Maghdel Zoun, Mansouri and Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon.

threads.label: Iran domestic economy and factional debate
threads.summary: Government spokesman Mohajerani said the petrol decision is not finalised, noting Iran converts eight million barrels of oil equivalent daily into fuel products, while Iran International reported households borrowing for medicine as authorities prioritise Arbaeen healthcare. Iran International and Defa Press both flagged a Tehran split over whether to negotiate with Washington, with Deputy Speaker Hajibaba'i saying no understanding with America will be reached.

events.title_en: Claim of woman killed at Alikhani Square in Isfahan is false
events.summary_en: The claim of a woman being killed at Alikhani Square in Isfahan is false. For some hours, claims have been circulated in cyberspace by some hostile media outlets stating that a woman with known identity was killed in the surroundings of Alikhani Square in Isfahan last night. According to a statement from the Isfahan judiciary, the aforementioned claim is false and no report has been received of a woman with the stated identity being killed in the location in question.

events.title_en: Consolidating Baghdad's position in the region without mediation between Tehran and Washington
events.summary_en: Ali al-Zidawi's visit to Tehran, immediately after his presence in Washington, sparked speculation about Iraq's possible role in mediating between Iran and America. However, Iraq is more concerned with consolidating its political and security weight in regional equations than being in the position of a neutral mediator. Iran-Iraq relations cannot be understood without returning to 1979, the year when the triumph of the Islamic Revolution in Iran caused the entire political and security balance of the region to shift. From that point, Baghdad-Tehran relations entered a phase of tension, instability and hostility, a process that ultimately led to the eight-year war.

events.title: The commander of Hamas's internal security forces in the central Gaza Strip was killed in an Israeli strike yesterday, the military announces. The strike targeting a car in Deir al-Balah killed Wael al-Ladawi, the commander of Hamas's Internal Security Service in the central governorate. Hamas's interior ministry announced his death yesterday. The military says the security service under Ladawi "collected intelligence for senior Hamas officials, supporting their decision-making and facilitating the planning and execution of terrorist attacks against the State of Israel."

events.title: Updating Website and Contact Information, and Authorizations for Payments for Legal Services
events.summary: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is adopting a final rule to update website and contact information in certain parts of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). Additionally, OFAC is amending one CFR Part to update general licenses authorizing payments for legal services from funds originating outside the United States to replace the reporting requirement in the general license with a recordkeeping requirement and correcting typographical errors in two CFR Parts. OFAC is also updating its regulations to correct an erroneous cross-reference.

details.agencies: Treasury Department, Foreign Assets Control Office
